newsitem.title: CANADA: Wages, low dollar to push Canadian export growth.
newsitem.headline: Wages, low dollar to push Canadian export growth.

text.p: Competitive wage costs and a low Canadian dollar will boost Canadian exports by 7.5 percent in 1997 and by 7.3 percent annually until the year 2003, said Canada's export credit agency on Wednesday.

The Export Development Corp (EDC) predicted exports to the United States, Canada's largest trading partner, would grow 7.7 percent in 1997, while the amount of Canadian goods destined for Asia would jump 8.4 percent.
Exports to Western Europe will increase by 4.8 percent this year, and sales to Latin America will edge upward by 7.2 percent, the EDC said.

"While exporters cannot expect a return to the double digit growth of the mid 1990s, they will continue to enjoy a healthy growth in sales due to ongoing competitiveness and continuing strong market demand," said Jim Olts, EDC's chief economist.
"The U.S. is now experiencing the golden years of its expansion," Olts said. "Business conditions are about as close to optimum as they can be."
Capital and industrial goods, rather than resource-based exports, will benefit the most from the export growth in 1997, the EDC said.
